workflows.name: quantification_analysis
workflows.intent: Estimate transcription rates for each enhancer and test for activity against negative controls.
workflows.stages:
1. Initialize the MpraObject with count matrices, annotations, and control identifiers.
2. Estimate library depth normalization factors.
3. Fit the quantification model using DNA and RNA design formulas.
4. Extract transcription rate estimates (alpha values).
5. Test for enhancer activity against negative controls using empirical testing.
workflows.code:
obj <- MpraObject(dnaCounts = ce.dnaCounts, rnaCounts = ce.rnaCounts, 
                  dnaAnnot = ce.colAnnot, rnaAnnot = ce.colAnnot, 
                  controls = ce.control)
obj <- estimateDepthFactors(obj, lib.factor = c("batch", "condition"),
                            which.lib = "both")
obj <- analyzeQuantification(obj = obj, 
                              dnaDesign = ~ batch + condition,
                              rnaDesign = ~ condition)
alpha <- getAlpha(obj, by.factor = "condition")
res.epi <- testEmpirical(obj = obj, 
                               statistic = alpha$MT)

workflows.name: comparative_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify enhancers that are differentially active between conditions or alleles using a nested GLM and likelihood ratio test.
workflows.stages:
1. (Optional) Create interaction factors for barcode and condition if performing allelic/mutagenesis comparisons where barcodes are not shared.
2. Initialize the MpraObject.
3. Estimate library depth normalization factors.
4. Fit the comparative models (full and reduced) using DNA, RNA, and reduced design formulas.
5. Perform a Likelihood Ratio Test to identify differentially active enhancers.
workflows.code:
ce.colAnnot$barcode_allelic <- interaction(ce.colAnnot$barcode, ce.colAnnot$condition)
obj <- MpraObject(dnaCounts = ce.dnaCounts, rnaCounts = ce.rnaCounts, 
                  dnaAnnot = ce.colAnnot, rnaAnnot = ce.colAnnot, 
                  controls = ce.control)
obj <- estimateDepthFactors(obj, lib.factor = c("batch", "condition"),
                            which.lib = "both")
obj <- analyzeComparative(obj = obj, 
                           dnaDesign = ~ barcode + batch + condition, 
                           rnaDesign = ~ condition, 
                           reducedDesign = ~ 1)
res <- testLrt(obj)

workflows.name: scalable_comparative_analysis
workflows.intent: Run a fast comparative analysis on large datasets with matched DNA/RNA observations by using DNA counts directly instead of fitting a DNA model.
workflows.stages:
1. Initialize the MpraObject.
2. Estimate library depth normalization factors.
3. Fit the comparative models in scalable mode (mode="scale") without a DNA design.
4. Perform a Likelihood Ratio Test to identify differentially active enhancers.
workflows.code:
obj <- MpraObject(dnaCounts = ce.dnaCounts, rnaCounts = ce.rnaCounts, 
                  dnaAnnot = ce.colAnnot, rnaAnnot = ce.colAnnot, 
                  controls = ce.control)
obj <- estimateDepthFactors(obj, lib.factor = c("batch", "condition"),
                            which.lib = "both")
obj <- analyzeComparative(obj = obj, 
                          rnaDesign = ~ condition, 
                          reducedDesign = ~ 1, 
                          mode="scale")
res.scale <- testLrt(obj)
